place_fields.vibe: Scenic mountain viewpoint with a short summit climb
place_fields.summary: Mullayanagiri is Karnataka's highest peak at about 1,930 metres. The summit is accessible by road, followed by a short climb of about 500 steps from the parking area, with views over the Western Ghats.
place_fields.best_time: September to March is the clearest recommended period; monsoon brings greener scenery but can reduce road visibility.

planning_attributes.description: A high-elevation peak and popular hill attraction in Chikkamagaluru, known for panoramic Western Ghats views and the Mullappa Swamy temple at the summit.
planning_attributes.legend_or_history: The summit temple is dedicated to Mullappa Swamy, and the peak's name is associated with the sage believed to have meditated in a cave near the summit.
planning_attributes.how_to_reach: Reach the Mullayanagiri area by road from Chikkamagaluru; the final approach includes a narrow road and a short stair climb from the parking area to the summit.
planning_attributes.access_restrictions: The summit temple is reported open 7 AM to 7 PM. The cave below the temple described by Karnataka Tourism is closed.
planning_attributes.safety_notes: The approach road is narrow and requires careful driving; monsoon conditions can reduce visibility and make access less comfortable.

place_fields.vibe: Green Western Ghats ridge trek with broad mountain views
place_fields.summary: Netravati Peak & Kallusanka Trek is a Western Ghats trekking route near Kalasa/Samse with forest, grassland and steep sections toward the higher portions of the trail.
place_fields.best_time: Post-monsoon and winter conditions are generally more suitable for clearer views; monsoon conditions can make sections slippery.

planning_attributes.description: A trekking route associated with Netravati Peak in the Kudremukh landscape of Chikkamagaluru district, combining forested sections, grasslands and ridge views.
planning_attributes.elevation_or_height: Sources consulted place the peak in the approximately 1,250–1,520 metre range; the exact elevation is not consistently reported.
planning_attributes.legend_or_history: The Netravati River originates in the broader Kudremukh landscape; the exact historical origin claim for this named trek was not independently established.
planning_attributes.how_to_reach: The route is associated with the Kalasa/Samse side of the Kudremukh region; access to the trailhead may involve local road or jeep transport.
planning_attributes.access_restrictions: Trek reports indicate advance booking/limited forest permits may apply; confirm current permission requirements before travel.
planning_attributes.safety_notes: Steep and slippery sections can occur, especially in wet weather. Trekking footwear with good grip and attention to trail conditions are advisable.
planning_attributes.notes: Published sources differ on exact elevation and trek distance; those figures were not treated as definitive.

place_fields.vibe: Quiet hill viewpoint with panoramic Western Ghats scenery
place_fields.summary: Seethalayyanagiri is a smaller hill on the way to Mullayanagiri and can be visited as part of the same mountain circuit.
place_fields.best_time: September to March is the recommended clearer-weather period for the surrounding Chikkamagaluru hills; monsoon conditions can bring mist and reduced visibility.

planning_attributes.description: A smaller hill attraction associated with the Mullayanagiri route in Chikkamagaluru, offering access to the surrounding Western Ghats landscape.
planning_attributes.legend_or_history: Karnataka Tourism notes a reported cave connection between the Mullayanagiri and Seethalayyanagiri temples, but the cave is now closed.
planning_attributes.how_to_reach: It lies on the route to Mullayanagiri and can be combined with a visit to Mullayanagiri and nearby Baba Budangiri attractions.
planning_attributes.access_restrictions: The reported cave connection is closed; no additional current restriction was established from the sources consulted.
planning_attributes.safety_notes: Mountain roads in the Mullayanagiri area can be narrow; monsoon weather may reduce visibility and make road travel less comfortable.
